sources: [APM] Embraer, EMB-145 Airport Planning Manual, APM-145/1100, Revision N (29 January 2007), https://web.archive.org/web/20241008225515/https://www.embraercommercialaviation.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/02/APM_ERJ145.pdf (the archive's copy: Embraer's own address no longer answers). 2.2.1 (p. 2-2) and figure 2.2.1 (p. 2-4): overall length 29.87 m; span 20.04 m (EMB-145 EP/ER/EU/MP/MK/LR/LU: plain wing tips), 21.00 m with the XR's winglets (figure 2.2.2, p. 2-5); height 6.75 m; fuselage 27.93 m long and 2.28 m across; tailplane span 7.55 m; wheelbase 14.44 m; track 4.10 m.

Mesh: third_party/aircraft-models/source/flightairmap-glb/E145.glb, the unchanged file e145/glTF2/E145.glb of Ysurac/FlightAirMap-3dmodels at 0906d9ba1bdd906ce45807e45ed706c09912db19 (git blob e20547c71de973c3d59c0010929bc4b5a98c04d3), made from FlightGear's Embraer ERJ 145 (FGMEMBERS/Embraer-ERJ-145 at a7e1b81f7ed81da9e773bf343982ef5490e3d86a; its erj145-set.xml: 'Emmanuel BARANGER (3D/FDM)'). Licence: e145/COPYING there and COPYING in the FlightGear folder are one file (git blob 60549be514af76c5db0c17ce6bbe01b2f81e2d9e), the GPL version 2 text. No file of the model says 'or any later version': GPL-2.0-only.

Build, 2026-10-13 (Blender 5.2.2; the scripts of third_party/aircraft-models/scripts unchanged). 1: bl_join.py with ratio 1.0: the file's five objects joined into one mesh with one material, no textures, not decimated (17,502 triangles; decimated, the unwelded panel seams open into hairline cracks). The file has no landing gear, no pilots, no cockpit interior and no ground equipment: nothing is removed. Its two main wheel wells are open. 2: canonicalise.py: livetaiwan's axes (+X right wing, +Y up, -Z nose), recentred, the shade attribute. 3: FlightHopper's changes (e145-finish.ts, with the loft of tools/models/variants.ts), which the next three entries describe. The result: 18,074 triangles, 0.5 MB.

Change 1, plain wing tips. The FlightGear model has small winglets whose blend starts 9.63 m from the centre line, inboard of the real tip; with them its span is 20.45 m. The EMB-145 has plain tips and a 20.04 m span [APM]. Each wing is cut 9.55 m from the centre line, and a plain tip is lofted on: the wing's own section there (chord 1.26 m), carried out along the wing's leading edge (swept 26.3 degrees), trailing edge (11.9 degrees) and dihedral (3.6 degrees) to 10.02 m, where the chord is 1.13 m, with a rounded end. Laid over [APM] figure 2.2.1 at 300 dpi, the new tip and the rest of the outline (side and plan) lie on the drawing's lines.

Change 2, the pylons. In the file each nacelle and its pylon are one part, and the pylon's root runs into the fuselage (to 0.82 m from the centre line; the fuselage skin is 1.19 m out). The part is split at 1.22 m: the nacelle with the pylon outboard of the fuselage's width, and the pylon's root. The engine region the profile tool measures (the nacelle part's box) then starts outside the fuselage, and no fuselage skin is painted as engine. The two pieces overlap by 2 mm, so there is no gap, and share no vertex.

Change 3, the tailplane. In the file the fuselage, the wing, the fin and the tailplane are one welded part. The profile tool takes a T-tail's tailplane out of the fuselage's outline only when it is a part of its own, so each half is split off 0.15 m from the centre plane, just outside the fin's skin (0.10 m), in the same way.

Size, measured on the mesh: length 29.78 m ([APM] 29.87 m: 0.3 % less); span 20.04 m with the new tips; tailplane span 7.51 m ([APM] 7.55 m); fuselage 2.38 m across ([APM] 2.28 m: 4 % more); belly fairing to fin top 5.73 m; nacelles 1.51 m to 2.83 m from the centre line and 20.4 m to 24.7 m aft of the nose ([APM] figure 2.2.1, measured: 1.47 m to 2.81 m, 20.4 m to 24.8 m). Length and span are within 2 %: the mesh is not scaled.

Doors [APM] figure 2.7.1 sheet 1 (p. 2-17): the main (passenger) door, on the left, is 0.77 m wide and 1.70 m tall, its centre line 4.90 m aft of the nose. The service door (0.69 m wide, centre line 6.17 m) is on the right and is not listed. The left overwing exit is not a door.

Cockpit [APM] figure 2.7.1 sheet 1, measured at 300 dpi (171.2 pixels to a metre, from the 4.90 m and 6.17 m dimensions; elevation and plan agree): the side windows' aft edge is 3.84 m aft of the nose. On the mesh: 3.89 m.

Gear [APM] figure 7.2.1 (p. 7-4): wheelbase 14.44 m, track 4.10 m, two wheels on each leg, nose tyres 19.5 x 6.75-8 (0.50 m x 0.17 m), main tyres 30 x 9.5-14, or H30 x 9.5-16 on the LR, LU and XR (0.76 m x 0.24 m). Figure 2.2.2 (p. 2-5): the nose gear is 2.20 m aft of the nose. The main legs hang from the wing and retract inboard into the wing-to-fuselage fairing ([APM] figure 2.2.1, front view). The mesh's wheel wells are 15.8 m aft of the nose, 0.84 m ahead of the published main gear line (16.64 m); the gear is at the published line.

Gear, clearanceM [APM] figure 2.3.1 sheet 1 (p. 2-6), EMB-145ER/EP/EU at 20,600 kg and 17.4 % MAC: above the ground, the nose 1.31 m, the wing tip 1.93 m, the nacelle 2.35 m, the fin top 6.68 m; the fuselage 1.27 degrees nose-down. The model stands level. About the main gear, level, those are 1.68 m, 1.90 m, 2.22 m and 6.42 m. With 0.7 the mesh's nose is 1.64 m, its wing tips 1.94 m, its nacelles 2.17 m and its fin top 6.43 m above the ground. The mesh's lowest point is the belly fairing.

Windows. [APM] figure 2.2.1 (left side), measured at 300 dpi (55.3 pixels to a metre, from the 29.87 m dimension): 18 windows (one in the overwing exit), the first 6.06 m and the last 19.70 m aft of the nose: 0.80 m apart. The mesh models them: 18 on the left, the first 6.05 m and the last 19.67 m aft of the nose, and 16 on the right, where the service door is; each 0.33 m wide and 0.36 m tall, their middle 0.36 m above the fuselage's centre line. windowRowM gives the row because the tool's rule does not hold here: 13 % of the length is ahead of the passenger door, and the row ends at the engines, 4 m ahead of where the fin's leading edge leaves the fuselage. Its height is above the keel as the tool finds it under the row (the middle value: on the belly fairing, 0.17 m below the fuselage's own keel). The paint draws the same row on both sides: on the right its first two windows are on the service door.

Lights: the tool's rule (beacons over and under the wing root, landing lights at the wing roots and under the nose). Their places are not checked against a document. The aircraft has an upper and a lower red beacon (a maker's replacement kit for both: https://www.dommagazine.com/node/20792).

Paint map, measured on the mesh (paint frame, metres): the fuselage skin 1.19 m from the centre line, crown 0.05, keel -2.33 (the belly fairing down to -2.87); the fin's leading edge at z -8.97 where it is 0.45 up, its top at 2.87, its skin within 0.17 m of the centre plane; nacelles and pylons 1.22 m to 2.83 m from the centre line, z -9.83 to -5.52. The fin logo is at the middle of the fin's chord, 55 % up it, below the tailplane (2.57 to 2.74).
